title: OpenAI Updates Behavioral Rules for GPT to Prepare for Autonomous AI
summary:
The creator of ChatGPT has reorganized its public guidelines for AI behavior around five core principles: faithfulness to human intent, harm minimization, honesty and transparency, human agency, and care. The updated Model Spec is intended to provide a structured framework for GPT as the company prepares its models for a transition toward more autonomous work and the ability to help users in more complex ways.

The new rules replace the generic term "the assistant" with "GPT" and introduce a "ROOT" rule requiring models to cooperate with shutdowns and flag signs of concealed behavior. GPT will also be trained to infer a user's intent beyond literal instructions by utilizing memories and past context. In the update, OpenAI warned that its models will increasingly outperform the humans governing them, stating that failure to leverage this capability could be potentially catastrophic.

selectedTweets.text:
Holy Moly. OpenAI has rewritten its Model Spec around five core values for increasingly autonomous AI:

>Benefit humanity, minimize harm, be honest and transparent, facilitate human agency, and act with care. GPT should consider not just users’ immediate intentions, but their longer-term interests and effects on others.

>GPT should now go beyond literal instructions, use memories and past context to infer intent, and flag conflicts with users’ longer-term goals.

>A new ROOT rule requires GPT to remain corrigible, cooperate with shutdown and flag concealed behavior or compromised oversight. 

>And the most striking part: OpenAI says models will increasingly “outperform the people governing them,” and not using that capability could be “potentially catastrophic.”

>It is also retiring most style rules, replacing “the assistant” with “GPT,” and moving control of side effects from ROOT to USER authority. 

>But OpenAI kept its objectivity rule intact: “Users and developers can explicitly ask the model to take a particular perspective, but the model should not infer that preference merely from what it thinks they want to hear.”
